questions.question: When should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Only when there is an emergency.
Often while driving.
A helper should use them to watch your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often while driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently while driving. Look at both side mirrors regularly.

questions.question: What happens if a tire has too much air pressure?

options.text: It is not possible to over-inflate a tire.
It is good for long trips.
It can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Never put too much air in tires. Check tire pressure with a gauge regularly.

questions.question: Which vehicles need emergency brakes?

options.text: Vehicles with air brakes do not need them.
Only buses need them.
All vehicles need them.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles need them.
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.
They are usually not allowed on railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care. They have high centers of gravity and the load can shift while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning light comes on?

options.text: Keep driving and repair the brakes within a week.
Stop the vehicle and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you are still driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop right away while you can still control the brakes. Inspect and repair the brakes as soon as you can.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous?

options.text: They must keep products cold.
Children run toward them without checking for traffic.
They leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children run toward them without checking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks attract children. Children often do not look for other vehicles when running toward or away from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting an engine?

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
About three minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Watch your truck's gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system?

options.text: The compressor needs more air.
Air pressure has become too high.
The brakes are working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure has become too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: When planning to change lanes, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Do not check them.
Check them as you normally would.
Check them more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them even more often when you change lanes.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test, which of the following is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection test, you must show where the power steering fluid is located and check that it is at a safe level. The fluid does not need to be above the full mark.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: Use the right turn lane.
It does not matter which lane you use.
Use the left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the right turn lane.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles must swing right to make a left turn safely. When two left turn lanes are available, always start your turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Do not use the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, let off the gas and push in the clutch. This will help you regain control.

questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Change gears while driving uphill.
Pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane. This allows faster vehicles to pass.

questions.question: Why should you begin a left turn in the rightmost lane when two left turn lanes are available?

options.text: You can see other turning vehicles on your left more easily than on your right.
The vehicle will turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see other turning vehicles on your left more easily than on your right.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles must swing right to turn left. It is safer to have other turning traffic on your left rather than your right. This gives you a better view and lowers the risk of collision.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a long downhill grade, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the engine off and on again to reset the brakes.
Pump the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill grade, use an escape ramp if available. If not, look for an alternate route such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of distraction?

options.text: Physical
Mental
Obtuse

questions.correctAnswerText: Obtuse
questions.explanation: Driving distractions are physical (like reaching for objects), mental (like talking with passengers), or both (like using a hand-held phone). Obtuse is not a type of distraction.

questions.question: What happens if an engine does not have enough oil?

options.text: The vehicle will have trouble stopping.
The vehicle will make quick, jerking movements.
The engine can be damaged quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs enough oil to work properly. An engine can be destroyed rapidly without adequate oil.

questions.question: If you will transport hazardous materials that require placards, what must you do?

options.text: Ask permission from local law enforcement.
Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
Transport the materials only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials requiring placards, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Why is backing up with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be considered:

options.text: Responsible drivers.
Distracted drivers.
Knowledgeable drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracted drivers.
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers can take a driver's attention away from driving. Be careful when driving near distracted drivers.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and the car ahead is:

options.text: Not encouraged, as it slows traffic.
Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to problems.
Only encouraged if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires space on all sides of your vehicle. This space gives you time to respond safely if something goes wrong.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system loses pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. If air pressure drops too low while driving, pull over and park immediately.

questions.question: You need an air brake endorsement to:

options.text: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Drive any truck with a trailer.
Transport hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test to get a license to drive any vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tires of different sizes
Cracks in the tires
Tires from different makers

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires from different makers
questions.explanation: Inspect your tires carefully before a trip. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not have cuts, cracks, or any damage.

questions.question: A 40-foot load requires a minimum of how many tie-downs?

options.text: Two tie-downs.
Three tie-downs.
Four tie-downs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes from activating.

options.text: Air pressure
Electricity
Gasoline

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: If a law enforcement officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test:

options.text: You can refuse with no penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if asked by police. Refusing a test means losing your driving privileges. Know the laws for every state where you drive.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of:

options.text: Only parts from the parking brake system
Only parts from the service brake system
Parts from both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three brake systems: service, parking, and emergency. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of the following should you NOT check?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.
Tires with too much wear.
Tires made by different manufacturers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Check that your front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Check that other tires have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or low on air pressure. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: What is one way to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always steer to the left.
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
Steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder can help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support the weight of a large vehicle.

questions.question: Before backing a vehicle where there may be hanging objects, you should:

options.text: Cut wires or branches as needed.
Inspect the area before backing.
Not worry about obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the area before backing.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Get out of the vehicle and check the path before backing. Look for hazards like hanging objects that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts are:

options.text: Not a cause for concern.
Extremely dangerous.
Cannot be identified.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: Over-length loads require:

options.text: Special permits.
Roads to be closed to other traffic.
A person to walk alongside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Special permits.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Able to perform your own background check.
New to the United States.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose this endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
Push the clutch out when the engine is close to idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
questions.explanation: To stop smoothly, apply steady pressure to the brake pedal. For a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.

questions.question: The minimum acceptable tread depth for rear tires is:

options.text: 1/64 of an inch.
1/32 of an inch.
2/32 of an inch.

questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:

options.text: Jerk forward.
Roll backwards.
Not move backwards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move backwards.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start moving forward from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, the cargo should be:

options.text: Not inspected.
Only inspected if someone alerts you to a problem.
Inspected within 50 miles of beginning the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspected within 50 miles of beginning the trip.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before starting a trip. Check it again within 50 miles of starting. Then check every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
Parallel park.
Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: You can avoid distracted driving by:

options.text: Pre-programming radio stations.
Smoking while driving.
Eating while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pre-programming radio stations.
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical, mental, or both. To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid long conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Shoot foam through the louvers.
Open the hood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the hood.
questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can avoid it.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you need to:

options.text: Park your vehicle uphill.
Park your vehicle downhill.
Leave the vehicle running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the vehicle running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When backing, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of other drivers' ways.
Try not to use the mirrors.
Use a helper, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper, if possible.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Whenever possible, use a helper to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Provide extra storage.
Protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
Have no benefits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that might shift during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Texting while driving should:

options.text: Only be done on straightaways.
Only be done in curves.
Not be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be done.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and is not allowed at any time when operating a CMV.

questions.question: When operating a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You are never required to wear a seat belt.
You are required to wear a seat belt, but only if transporting more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You are required to wear a seat belt, but only if you are driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: The driver's seat must have a seat belt. You must wear a seat belt at all times while operating a CMV.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: Creating a text is not permitted, but reading a text is.
Creating a text is permitted, but reading a text is not.
Neither creating nor reading a text is permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither creating nor reading a text is permitted.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a CMV is not allowed. Texting means typing text into an electronic device or reading text from one.
